questions.q: What does Pema Chödrön say our experience of life depends on?
a: Whether we choose to see each moment with joy or as a burden
How much we achieve compared with other people
The amount of time we spend planning ahead
Whether our childhood was happy or difficult
questions.why: Lesson 1 says life is a string of small moments, and our experience hinges on how we choose to see them.

questions.q: Why does the summary describe emptiness as a good thing?
a: It releases us from labels and judgments that disturb our peace
It allows us to forget our responsibilities
It makes us more productive at work
It removes the need for other people
questions.why: Lesson 2 says emptiness frees you from labels and judgments that cloud your vision.

questions.q: What does the Zen story of the empty boat teach about anger?
a: We invent reasons to be angry that do not exist in reality
Anger is always a reasonable response to being wronged
We should confront the people who upset us directly
Boats are a common source of frustration in daily life
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the man shouted at an empty boat, just as we get angry at reasons we made up ourselves.

questions.q: How did the two dying friends in the summary differ?
a: One fought the void in despair while the other welcomed it in peace
One had family nearby while the other died alone
One was young and the other was elderly
One believed in rebirth while the other did not
questions.why: Lesson 2 contrasts resisting emptiness with accepting it, which changes how each person meets death.

questions.q: What benefit comes from letting go of the story you tell about yourself?
a: You stop worrying about looking foolish when you fall short
You become more certain about who you really are
You gain a clearer plan for the future
You no longer need to meditate each day
questions.why: Lesson 3 says dropping fixed beliefs about yourself removes the fear of embarrassment.
